newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby union-Williams rules out wholesale changes.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Williams rules out wholesale changes.

text.p: New South Wales rugby union coach Matt Williams has ruled out making wholesale team changes in the wake of his side's humiliating Super 12 drubbing by ACT Brumbies on Saturday.
"It would be the worst possible choice to make a whole lot of changes," said Williams, who must lift his demoralised mid-table outfit before the visit to Wellington on Friday.
"I am very loyal to my players. I don't think it would be a smart move to throw a lot of young players into a competition like the Super 12," Williams said.
New South Wales have come under intense fire since their 56-9 drubbing against the Brumbies, who ran in eight tries to nil at Bruce Stadium.
Veteran winger David Campese, flanker Michael Brial, front rower Phil Kearns and forward Fili Finau are all expected to return for the encounter with Wellington in Napier.
The Waratahs must win to keep alive their faint hopes of qualifying for the Super 12 semifinals by finishing in the top four at the end of the regular season.
"New South Wales rugby has also not been consistent week in and week out ... I'm not going to criticise any particular member of the team publicly," Williams said
"I'm the front man so I'll cop the criticism. We just have to pull together as a team."
